stem: A child with chronic fatty diarrhoea is thought to have inadequate pancreatic enzyme activity; which normal function is most directly reduced?

options.text: Hydrolysis of fat by gastric acid
Solubilisation of fat by bile salts
Direct portal venous entry of small- and medium-chain triglycerides
Absorption of vitamin B12 in the terminal ileum

explanation: Digestion of fat is the correct answer. Pancreatic enzymes are required for normal fat digestion, so inadequate pancreatic enzyme activity most directly reduces fat digestion.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Diarrhoea and Malabsorption

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because gastric acid is not the main mechanism for fat digestion
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because bile salts help emulsify and solubilise fat, but they are not pancreatic enzymes
optionExplanations.C: Correct because pancreatic enzymes are required for digestion of fat
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because small- and medium-chain triglycerides can enter the portal circulation directly, but this is a transport pathway rather than the main pancreatic function
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because vitamin B12 absorption is a separate intestinal process and is not the primary function reduced here
